JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed u/s166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 04.10.2022 at about 1.45 p.m, the petitioner along with his wife were proceeding on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HE- 0773 and was riding the same in slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Jain College, National School road, Bengaluru City at that time the driver of the Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 drove the same in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life came from opposite side and firstly the driver of car dashed to parked Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX- 7931, then on the same speed proceeding and dashed against the scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HE-0773 which the petitioner and his wife were proceeding and again dashed against another SCCH-23 scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-KF-6093.
Due to the terrific impact he and his wife fell down from the scooter and sustained grievous injuries Vijaya Bhaskaran.

2 on their bodies.

Soon after the accident he was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopedic Centre, after first aid he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Swift car.

The respondent No.1 to 3 being the driver, owner and insurer of Swift car, the respondent No.4 and 5 are the owner and insurer of the Innova car and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
SCCH-23 3.
Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2 and 4.
Respondent No.2 and 4 appeared through their counsel, they failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.

5. The respondent No.3/Universal Sompo Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent has contended that the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

Further this respondent denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle and contended that the accident between the petitioner vehicle and the Innova car and motorcycle and there is no negligence of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460.
Without SCCH-23 prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. The respondent No.5/Royal Sundaram Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-7931.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent has contended that on the date of accident, the insured car was stationed on the left side of the road.

The driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, dashed against the insured car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-7931 and thereafter dashed against the scooter which was ridden by the petitioner.
SCCH-23
Hence the accident took place solely due to the negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460.

The police after investigation have filed charge sheet against the Vijaya Bhaskaran.K vs Tanish Jain on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148761555/
3 driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460.
Hence petition requires to be rejected as against this respondent.
7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 04.10.2022 at about 1.45 p.m., near Jain College, National School Road, Bengaluru City due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
3) What order or award ?
8. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to 16 and Ex.P.20 were marked on his behalf.
Dr.Krishan Prasad was examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.17 to 19 documents.
Further the petitioner also examined his employer as PW.3.
In order to prove the defence, respondent No.5 insurance company SCCH-23 got examined its concerned officer as RW.1.
Ex. R.1
& 2 were marked through him.
9. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondents No.3 & 5 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 : The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioner and respondent No.5 plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460.

Whereas the respondent No.1 to 3 being the driver, owner and insurer of Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 contends that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the driver of Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-7931.
SCCH-23 11.
The petitioner in order to prove his case himself examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination affidavit evidence he reiterated the averments of petition.
Advocate for respondent No.3 cross examined the PW.1, but nothing has been elicited against the charge sheet and other documentary Vijaya Bhaskaran.

on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148761555/
4 evidence.
12. In order to prove the defence the respondent No.5/Royal Sundaram Gen. Ins.co. examined its official as RW.1.
He reiterated the averments of written statement filed by respondent No.5.
He stated that the insured car was stationed on the left side of the road.

The driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-MH-8460 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, dashed against the insured car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-7931 and thereafter dashed against the scooter which was ridden by the petitioner.
Hence the accident took place solely due to the negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-MH-8460 and police have filed charge sheet against the driver of swift car.

13. The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Sri. Mahesh Kumar, the jurisdictional SCCH-23 police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 for the offences punishable u/s's 279 & 337 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Though PW.1 cross examined at length by respondent No.5 counsel wherein he categorically admitted that the accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 and the police have also filed charge sheet against the driver of above said car.
He stated that one car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-7931 was parked on the left side of the road.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.8- Spot sketch it clears that the driver of offending vehicle drove the car extreme right side i.e., wrong side and first dashed to the middle left portion of the Innova car and then went in same speed and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner on the opposite side again taken his vehicle on right side and dashed to the another motorcycle on opposite side.
As such this Court cannot found fault with the version of the petitioner herein.

Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to SCCH-23 have been caused only due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-7931.
On assessing entire evidence and in the light of oral and documentary proof, the preponderance of probability tilts infavour of petitioner herein.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Swift car.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
15. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has exhibited his Aadhar card at Ex.P15,
wherein his date of birth is reflected as 16.08.1971.
This indicates that he was aged (51 years 1 months 19 days) 51 years on the date of accident.

16. The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident he was working as a Salesman at M/s Shadow Company which deals with wholesale Ready made Cloth business and was SCCH-23 earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and also entitled to other perks and benefits under the employment.
In order to substantiate the above said fact he has produced letter issued by Shadow Company.
Except oral evidence he has not produced any documents to show the income and avocation except Ex.P.12.
The petitioner in order to substantiate the income might have produced the statement of account or examine the author of Ex.P.12.

Vijaya Bhaskaran.K vs Tanish Jain on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148761555/
5 17.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has also examined the Proprietor of the said concern viz., Sri. Syed Muhammed Fayid as PW.3.
In order to test the veracity of the letter issued by his concern which is exhibited at Ex.P.12.
The PW.3 stated that the petitioner was working with him as a sales man and was working with their concern prior to the accident for a period of three years.
He paid the salary to the petitioner for a sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m during the employment.
He stated that subsequent to the accident, he had came for work, but he could not work as he was working prior to the accident hence he has been terminated from service.
The cross examination of SCCH-23 PW.3 was deferred on the request.
In view of above elicitations, no credence can be attached to the ocular evidence adduced by PW.3.
Even otherwise except Ex.P.12 nothing else is placed on record to show the petitioner was paid a monthly salary of Rs.25,000/-.

In the absence of authentic proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age and nature of his work, it is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
SCCH-23
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, Rs.15,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
18. As per the medical records petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Left distal end radius fracture.
It is needless to say that the injury is grievous in nature.

The discharge summary (Ex.P.5)
indicates that the petitioner was taken treatment as an inpatient from 04.10.2022 to 06.10.2022 for a period of 3 days.
During the course of treatment he undergone surgeries in the form of : Left distal end radius ORIF with VLP (6 holed VLP Nebula).
19. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Krishan Prasad as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total SCCH-23 residual physical disability of 40% to the upper limb and 14% disability to the whole body.
During the course of cross examination PW.2 admitted that he was not treated the petitioner and was assessed only disability.
He stated that as per X-ray the fracture has been united and the alignment is in good condition.
He stated that after his examination, fracture was united but one screw bone is getting eaten away.

He further stated that there is no loss of power and he was not Vijaya Bhaskaran.K vs Tanish Jain on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148761555/
6 under any external support.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.

Considering the SCCH-23 nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 9%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 9%.
20.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 3 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.3,600/- (1,200 X 3) is awarded under this head 21.
PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Having regard to the fractures suffered by the petitioner to weight bearing bones and such other attending SCCH-23 circumstances.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 3 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.46,500/- (15,500 X 3) under this head.
23. MEDICAL EXPENSES :
As per the bills marked at Ex.P16 and Ex.P.20 the petitioner has spent Rs.1,18,857/- and Rs.2,560/-, in total Rs.1,21,417/- towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross- examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,21,400/- towards medical expenses.
24. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is SCCH-23 '11'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,84,140/- (Rs.15,500 X 12 X 11 X 9/100) which is rounded off to Rs.1,84,200/- is awarded under this head.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is Vijaya Bhaskaran.K vs Tanish Jain on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148761555/
7 awarded under this head.
26. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which he may require Rs.75,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.
SCCH-23 27.

The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 3,600-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain &
sufferings : 50,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 46,500-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 1,21,400-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 1,84,200-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : 40,000-00 Total 4,95,700-00 28.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
29. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 to 3 being the driver, owner and insurer of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
SCCH-23
However the respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Further the petition hereby dismissed against the respondent No.4 & 5.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
30.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,95,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.3 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

Vijaya Bhaskaran.K vs Tanish Jain on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148761555/
8

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through SCCH-23 NEFT/
RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.

The petition is dismissed against respondent 4 & 5.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Further the respondent has contended that on the date of accident, the insured car was stationed on the left side of the road.
opennyai_summary.issue:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 04.10.2022 at about 1.45 p.m., near Jain College, National School Road, Bengaluru City due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
3) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
As such this Court cannot found fault with the version of the petitioner herein.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to SCCH-23 have been caused only due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-7931.
In the absence of authentic proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age and nature of his work, it is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
SCCH-23
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, Rs.15,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
It is needless to say that the injury is grievous in nature.
During the course of treatment he undergone surgeries in the form of : Left distal end radius ORIF with VLP (6 holed VLP Nebula).
19. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.
Considering the SCCH-23 nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 9%, cannot be ruled out.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
29. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 to 3 being the driver, owner and insurer of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MH-8460 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
SCCH-23
However the respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Further the petition hereby dismissed against the respondent No.4 & 5.
Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

ISSUE NO.3:
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,95,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.3 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.
Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through SCCH-23 NEFT/
RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
The petition is dismissed against respondent 4 & 5.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
